notes: Contraction paired with grammar-replace-0013. Removes the revision's original fact, the Russian language is officially written in the Cyrillic alphabet (cardinality:many has_official_script, stored). Russian has only one official script, so no second held value of has_official_script exists; the cardinality item instead asks the super-property written_in_script, which the model holds as its own stored fact and which removal of the official-script value leaves untouched (yes before and after). Topic limitation: a many-valued contraction here would need a subject with two official scripts, such as Serbian. Related near is the inverse form (official_script_of), which routes through the removed fact; the revision's written_in_script near question was dropped because that super-property survives the removal. Related far reuses the Bulgarian question. Derived: the script of the official language of Russia and whether Ukrainian shares the script (both composition). The revision's Q and Polish questions were not reused because their no-answers would survive the removal. The super-property fact is backed by Wikipedia, Russian language: 'Russian is written using the Russian alphabet of the Cyrillic script'.
